info.description:
getproperty — ให้เช่าง่าย อยู่สบาย, operated by Collective Group (Thailand) (D-001).
Rules: `docs/contract/api-conventions.md` (shared with getproperty-web and getproperty-edge); MQTT payloads: `docs/contract/device-protocol.md` / `contract/device-protocol.json` (D-130).

- **Surfaces:** `/v1/auth`, `/v1/owner` (operator), `/v1/staff` (operator, Staff role), `/v1/resident` (resident), `/v1/technician` (technician, R2), `/v1/admin` (platform), `/v1/device` (device), `/webhooks`, `/v1/public` (anonymous marketing reads). A token is accepted only on its own audience's prefix.
- **Tenancy:** a *tenant* is the SaaS customer organisation (D-151). Every owner/staff request runs in one tenant (`tenant:<uuid>` scope or `X-Tenant-Id`); a cross-tenant id is a 404 (contract §8, D-152).
- **Money:** decimal strings with exactly 2 decimals (`"1234.50"`) plus `currency: "THB"` on the object; never JSON numbers. Clients never compute prices (D-046).
- **Meter quantities:** `register` and `units` are decimal strings with up to 3 decimals (`"12345.678"`), `unit` is `kwh | m3`; tariff `pricePerUnit` has up to 4 decimals.
- **Dates:** ISO 8601 with offset, rendered in `Asia/Bangkok` (`2026-11-01T00:00:00+07:00`); date-only fields `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **IDs:** uuid only; business keys (`invoiceNumber`, `unitNo`, `deviceSerial`) are separate fields.
- **Errors:** RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`; `title`/`detail` localised by `Accept-Language` (`th` default, `en`). `compliance.*` refusals carry `legalRef` (D-020).
- **Lists:** `?page&perPage(≤100)&sort&order&q` → `{ data, meta: { page, perPage, total } }`; feeds use `?cursor&limit` → `{ data, meta: { nextCursor } }`; series take `from`, `to`, `bucket` (`15m | 1h | 1d`).
- **Idempotency:** irreversible POSTs require `Idempotency-Key` (uuid); replays within 24 h return the original response.
- **Concurrency:** editable resources return `ETag`; updates send `If-Match` (412 `concurrency.stale`).
- **Files:** presign → PUT to the returned URL → reference the `fileId`; downloads are short-lived signed URLs.

post.description:
For a building whose network blocks outbound 8883 (D-239, O-012 resolved): `wsFallback: true` lets the gateway connect over EMQX ws 8083 behind Caddy authenticated by its device JWT **alone** — no client certificate on that path, so a stolen JWT (≤ 1 h, issued only over mTLS to a non-retired gateway) is enough to connect for its lifetime. Off by default; the bootstrap answer and every `POST /v1/device/token` answer carry `mqtt.wsUrl` only for such a gateway, so a provisioned gateway picks the change up at its next token refresh (≤ 1 h, edge CR-015, D-249) — no new provisioning code. Only gateways, never retired ones; audited with the reason; the next WebSocket connect is decided by the new value.

Implements: D-235, D-239, D-249.

Audited.

post.description:
The gateway sends the one-time provisioning code from its QR (the serial is optional), a CSR (`CN=gw-provisioning` — the CA sets `CN=gw-<gatewayId>`), its agent version and hardware; the platform CA signs a client certificate (12 months, clientAuth), the broker ACL rows are written (publish only `gp/v1/<id>/telemetry`, `…/health`, `…/events`, `…/cmd/ack`; subscribe `…/config` and `…/cmd` — answered by the API’s EMQX HTTP authz, D-235), the MQTT password is the device JWT (protocol 1.2), `mqtt.wsUrl` appears only for a gateway whose WebSocket fallback the platform admin enabled (D-239), and a device session starts (JWT `aud=device` + refresh token, also as `deviceToken`). A second bootstrap of the same gateway revokes the previous certificate, ACL and sessions. Not idempotent by key: the code is single-use (second use → 401 `device.provisioning_code_invalid`); a lost response needs a new code (D-130, D-165, device protocol §1).

Implements: D-033, D-130, D-235, D-239, ADR-0003.
post.summary: Bootstrap a gateway: certificate, device JWT and broker ACL

post.description:
mTLS + device bearer: signs a CSR for a **new** key (`CN=gw-<gatewayId>`) with the platform CA; the old certificate stays valid until it expires and the agent reconnects MQTT with the new one. Due 11 months after `notBefore` or 30 days before `notAfter` (device protocol §1, CR-003). A certificate presented on the call must belong to the same gateway.

Implements: D-130, D-165.

get.description:
The latest compiled `GatewayConfig` of the calling gateway (device JWT, mTLS certificate of the same gateway when presented) — the same document published retained on `gp/v1/{gatewayId}/config`, for a cold start without MQTT. Shape: `GatewayConfig` of `contract/device-protocol.json` (D-131).

Implements: D-131, D-130.

post.description:
For the `upload_logs` command (device protocol §2): the gateway declares a gzip bundle (journal of the last hours + in-memory log ring, never secrets) with its size and SHA-256 and receives a short-lived PUT URL; the bundle becomes a `core.document` (kind `log_bundle`) of the gateway’s building, scanned like every upload. The agent then acks the command with `{ bytes, sha256 }` (CR-004, D-131).

Implements: D-131, D-130.

get.description:
The signed release artefact named by the manifest (`artifact.url` = `https://<DEVICE_HOST>/v1/device/ota/artifacts/<version>/<file>`), streamed from the product bucket (`releases/edge/<version>/<file>`, read-only for the app) to the calling gateway only — device JWT + its client certificate on the device host, a registered non-deprecated release of its architecture; anything else is a `404` (D-231, edge CR-012). The agent checks size and sha256 against the signed manifest before installing (D-131). No range requests; a broken download is restarted.

Implements: D-231, D-131.

200.description: The artefact bytes (`Content-Length` = the signed size, `ETag` = its sha256)

get.description:
The manifest of `releaseId` (the `ota_apply` URL) or of the latest rollout targeting the calling gateway, for its architecture only; the agent verifies the ed25519 signature with its baked-in keys before downloading (edge CR-011, D-131).

Implements: D-131.

get.description:
Answers with the surface name, the server time (Asia/Bangkok) and the API version. Placeholder operation of the `device` surface until its real endpoints land. Anonymous or with an `device` token (checked from B1.3: wrong audience → 403 `auth.wrong_audience`).

Implements: D-002, ADR-0002.

post.description:
Fallback when MQTT is unavailable (api-conventions §7): the body is a protocol `TelemetryBatch` of the calling gateway and goes through the same pipeline as MQTT — authorisation per meter channel, dedup on `(gatewayId, seqEpoch, meterId, seq)` (D-143, D-227: a re-flashed or replaced gateway sends a new `seqEpoch`), monthly partitions (D-162). Replays are harmless; an `Idempotency-Key` header is accepted and ignored (edge CR-009). Any 2xx means the readings are durable.

Implements: D-143, D-162, D-030, D-227.

Authenticated by the gateway’s client certificate alone (mTLS, no bearer): a certificate issued by the platform device CA, not revoked, within its validity, of a gateway that is not retired → a short-lived JWT (`aud=device`, `DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS`) in the gateway’s current session family. The agent refreshes one minute before `expiresAt` and never stores the token (CR-002, D-130, D-165). The answer also carries the gateway’s **current** MQTT endpoints (`mqtt { url, wsUrl? }`, edge CR-015, D-249): `wsUrl` is present only while the platform admin has this gateway’s WebSocket fallback on (D-239) and the platform publishes one — so switching the fallback on or off reaches an already-provisioned gateway at its next refresh, without a new provisioning code or a site visit. Additive within device protocol 1.2.

Implements: D-130, D-165, D-239, D-249.

With a ground and evidence (D-020): the lessor’s grounds need their notice period and the written notice on file (`compliance.termination_notice`); `lessee_notice` closes a lease the lessee gave notice for. **An `effectiveDate` after today records the lessor’s notice** (`200`, status `notice_given` — or still `ending` — with `notice.by = lessor`, the ground and the effective date): the lease, its occupancy, the unit and the resident’s door codes stay as they are until the hourly lifecycle sweep starts the move-out on that date; completing the move-out then closes it as `terminated` (D-219). An `effectiveDate` of today or earlier closes it now: occupancies close, the unit becomes vacant, the deposit settlement opens (D-023) and the resident’s door codes end with the lease (D-071, D-211). Never cuts power, and access never ends for arrears (D-024).

Implements: D-020, D-023, D-024, D-071, D-219.

post.description:
Requests a free slot of the listing’s availability (`GET /v1/public/listings/{slug}/viewing-slots`; notice and horizon are settings) — the owner confirms or declines. Opens the enquiry when there is none (same consent rule as asking). One live viewing per enquiry (`listing.viewing_exists`: change its time instead); a slot taken a moment ago answers `listing.viewing_slot_taken` (D-252). `mode: self` (G7, D-295) books a self-viewing slot: the listing must offer it (`viewing.self_unavailable` with the reason, `viewing.unit_occupied`), I must have a verified identity and phone and accept the visitor terms in force (`viewing.requirements_missing` with what is missing, `viewing.terms_outdated`), and no other self viewing of mine may overlap its code window (`viewing.access_overlap`).

Implements: D-252, D-025, D-295.
